title: Version-robust contract tests (IMP-8) and test report
story: As a maintainer I want contract tests that survive version bumps with actionable failure output, and a test report mapping requirements to proving tests, so releases do not break on cosmetic changes and coverage is auditable.
acceptance: yaml-lite.test.mjs no longer hard-codes '1.2.0': the expected info.version is read from the openapi.yaml text itself (independent regex) and compared to the parsed value, plus a semver-shape assertion; path-count assertions use a floor derived from the document, not a literal that breaks on bumps

routes.test.mjs keeps the snapshot comparison but the failure message prints the exact added/removed/changed operations as a diff and a one-line refresh command (e.g. node -e "import('./tests/security/routes.test.mjs').then(m=>m.refreshSnapshot())" or equivalent that works from the repo root)

routes.test.mjs exports a small refreshSnapshot() function that rewrites tests/security/routes.snapshot.json deterministically (sorted, same format); importing the module for the refresh does not run or break the tests; the header comment documents the command

Both test files pass: node --test --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning tests/unit/integrations/docs/yaml-lite.test.mjs tests/security/routes.test.mjs; a deliberate mutation (temporarily changing a snapshot entry in a scratch copy) shows the diff message

docs/test-report.md lists totals (suites, tests, pass, fail, todo, skipped) per suite folder from a full run of the suite with the date and command, and maps REQ-01..REQ-25 each to at least one named test file (or marks it as not automated with the reason)
brief: Part A (IMP-8, fast). yaml-lite.test.mjs line ~82 asserts doc.info.version equals '1.2.0': read the raw openapi text, extract the version with a regex such as /^\s{2}version:\s*(\S+)/m, assert it matches /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/ and equals doc.info.version; replace other literal counts with floors computed from a text count of operationId lines or a documented minimum. routes.test.mjs: the drift test currently uses two deepEquals with a generic message. Compute added, removed and changed (same op, different roles/module/public) and build a readable multi-line diff string (+ op / - op / ~ op old -> new). Throw via assert.fail with the diff and the refresh command. Add `export function refreshSnapshot()` that regenerates from parseOpenApi() in helpers.mjs using the same shape {op, roles, module, public} sorted by op, writing JSON with two-space indent and trailing newline; do not execute at import. Because test files run top-level code when imported, guard so importing for refresh is cheap (the tests register but the node:test runner is harmless outside --test; verify the command works). Document in the file header. Do not edit helpers.mjs or the snapshot file unless the refresh produces no change. Part B (docs, fast). Run the full suite once at the end: node --test --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning tests/**/*.test.mjs via a glob expanded by the shell (Node 22 rejects bare directories; also include tests/security/index.js if it is a test entry). Other teams may be mid-flight, so record the actual numbers and any failing test names honestly, never edit them to look green. Parse the TAP/spec summary per top-level folder (unit, integration, e2e, security, synthetic, ui). Map REQ-01..REQ-25 using product/requirements.md and grep the test names; include a note that dod.test.mjs and tenant-differences.test.mjs (S3-QE-01) are included if present at run time. Only synthetic data; no commits.

verdicts.reason: All 5 criteria verified: both files pass (58/0 fail), no hard-coded version, diff+refresh cmd message, refreshSnapshot exported, report has totals and REQ-01..25 map; 22 full-suite failures are outside ticket paths and documented
